guitar.modelsText: Gibson Les Paul (Joe Perry has a Bone Yard signature) / Brad Whitford Gibson Les Paul
models: Gibson Les Paul (Joe Perry has a Bone Yard signature)
guitar.evidence: Trained knowledge: Joe Perry is famously a Gibson Les Paul player (Billie Perry / Boneyard signatures), Brad Whitford also plays Les Pauls.
guitar.notes: Original was reasonable; refined to emphasize Les Paul as primary for both, dropped Strat mention as less central.

tone.target: dry late-70s hard-rock crunch with bright upper mids
tone.profile: dry late-70s hard-rock crunch with bright upper mids
tone.summary: A tight, crunchy signal chain utilizing a Boost for attack, an OD pedal for slight breakup, a UK 45 amp model, and the UK Vintage 4x12 cab to achieve a dry, aggressive late '70s hard rock sound.

blocks.purpose: Clean up pick noise and hum.
Tighten the attack and push the amp into a controlled crunch.
Provide slight, gritty breakup without heavy fuzz or metal gain.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is used as a general low-gain overdrive to simulate the light grit required, avoiding dedicated Tube Screamer models which were explicitly discouraged.

alternatives.reason: A slightly more versatile option for classic rock crunch.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the classic Marshall/Plexi sound required for late '70s hard rock.
Provide the classic British cabinet tone and frequency response.
Boost the upper mids and overall punch to achieve 'forward mids' and cut low-end mud.
Add a subtle, dry room ambience to glue the tone without sounding washed out.
blocks.gap: The requirement is for a 'dry mix,' so the Room effect must be used with very low wet levels (Mix: 0.2) and moderate decay time.

alternatives.reason: Could also provide subtle ambience, but Room better fits the dry hard rock context.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism by swapping the current IR for a more period-appropriate, high-mid focused British cab.

proposals.reason: Better captures the raw, aggressive mid-range punch of late '70s hard rock Plexi tones.
